cards.title: prompt() gives text
cards.body: `prompt()` always gives back text, even when the user types digits. Adding two pieces of text with `+` glues them together.

hi.title: prompt() text deta hai
hi.body: `prompt()` hamesha text hi deta hai, chahe user digits type kare. Do text ko `+` se jodo toh woh bas chipak jaate hain.

cards.title: Number() makes a number
cards.body: Wrap the text in `Number()` to turn it into a number. Then the maths works.

hi.title: Number() number banata hai
hi.body: Text ko `Number()` mein wrap karo toh woh number ban jaata hai. Phir maths sahi chalega.

cards.title: Maths operators
cards.body: `+`, `-`, `*` and `/` add, subtract, multiply and divide. As in school maths, `*` and `/` happen first; brackets change the order.

hi.title: Maths operators
hi.body: `+`, `-`, `*` aur `/` add, subtract, multiply aur divide karte hain. School maths ki tarah `*` aur `/` pehle hote hain; brackets order badal dete hain.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: Type 2 and 3 and it prints `23` instead of `5`. Which line is wrong?

bug.fix: `prompt()` gives text, and `+` with text joins instead of adding. Line 2 needs `Number(prompt())`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: 2 aur 3 type karo toh yeh `5` ki jagah `23` print karta hai. Kaunsi line galat hai?
hi.fix: `prompt()` text deta hai, aur text ke saath `+` add karne ki jagah jodta hai. Line 2 ko `Number(prompt())` chahiye.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: Both values are strings in quotes, so `+` glues them into 44.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: Dono values quotes mein strings hain, isliye `+` unhe chipka kar 44 bana deta hai.

exercise.prompt: Read two whole numbers, one per line, and print their sum.
exercise.promptHi: Do whole numbers padho, har line mein ek, aur unka sum print karo.
